title: Trace-backed incident summarizer and de-duplication
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Build a lightweight incident summarizer service that uses sampled traces and metric spikes to detect and consolidate duplicate alerts across latency/error dashboards. The goal is to reduce alert noise by grouping related symptoms (e.g., 99th percentile tail latency, request queueing, request timeouts, and downstream 5xx spikes) into a single summarized incident with ranked root-cause candidates and an automated suggested runbook. The summarizer will run as an offline scorer that annotates alerts before paging so routing rules can suppress duplicates and present a single actionable incident to oncall.
acceptance_criteria: Summarizer produces a human-readable incident summary for >90% of test incidents (benchmarked using synthetic fault runs)
Alert de-duplication reduces duplicate pages by >=40% in the staging tenant without delaying action on high-severity incidents
Summaries include top 3 RCA candidates with supporting traces/metrics links and confidence score
Rollout feature flag exists and can be toggled per-customer and per-model-route
No increase to page latency above 10% median vs baseline; tail increases must be within SLO tolerances
plan: Phase 0: Kickoff and data collection — capture representative trace samples, relevant metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, error counts), and historical alert payloads
Phase 1: Design summarization model — simple rule-based scorer + lightweight ML ranking based on feature vectors from traces and metric windows
Phase 2: Prototype service — implement scorer as idempotent lambda that annotates alert payload, returns summary + rca candidates
Phase 3: Integration — hook into existing alert pipeline (alert-router) to allow suppression and enrich pages with summary attachments
Phase 4: Canary rollout — enable for internal staging customers, monitor false-suppression rate and page-to-incident ratio
Phase 5: Gradual rollout to production with per-tenant toggles and audit logging
risks: False suppression could hide real incidents — mitigated by conservative thresholds and immediate rollback flag
Insufficient trace coverage may reduce RCA accuracy — fallback to metric-only summaries when traces unavailable
Extra processing could add latency to paging path — implement async scoring and attach summary without blocking critical paging
Privacy/compliance: traces may contain PII — ensure summarizer respects existing trace redaction rules
updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff — reviewed scope with PM and oncall leads. Decided to keep summarizer out of fast-path paging; will annotate and let router decide suppression.
2026-03-02: Data review — sampled traces show 18% coverage for the largest customer load; decided to fall back to aggregated metrics for low-coverage routes.
2026-03-05: Prototype complete — basic rule-based grouping implemented. Initial local tests show duplicate pages down 32% for synthetic noisy URL 123.
2026-03-09: Design review — security reviewed trace access; we added redaction enforcement and audit events. PM asked for per-tenant opt-out flag.
2026-03-12: Integration PR opened: alert-pipeline #482. Added acceptance test harness for synthetic fault injection and false-suppression monitoring. Assigned to Marcus for canary rollout planning.
notes: Trade-offs: Start with deterministic rules and simple ML reranker to keep behavior explainable for oncall. More advanced models (graph-based RCA) reserved for later phases.
Oncall UX: Summaries should include links to 1) representative trace span, 2) metric windows, 3) suggested runbook steps. Keep summary < 500 chars for pager body.
Alert routing policy: default is to suppress duplicate pages for 5 minutes but create a persistent incident in the console so metrics and timelines remain intact.
Testing: Use existing synthetic-probe harness from ENG-19765 to generate reproducible incidents and measure suppression/latency tradeoffs.
